answer: Give every new identity a voyage of probation instead of instant trust: it may only transact inside a small sandbox where established peers watch its work. To leave, it needs vouches from peers whose own standing would be cut if the newcomer cheats, so a vouch costs the giver real reputation. A willow bends for genuine newcomers, but a flood of fake identities faces the same wall again and again: each must separately earn watched work and vouches, and one detected fraud burns the whole cluster's vouches. A comet of quick fake accounts costs more to build than it can ever extract.
